In summary, our research is concerned with
how to best help physicians to be resilient.
how we as a profession can best help our trainees and colleagues become resilient, healthy physicians.
the impact of the medical school and residency training environment on the development of the future physician workforce.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the medical community has not done nearly enough to address the issues of physician wellbeing.
the medical education community has not yet fully embraced the need to address physician wellbeing and resilience as a critical component of the education and training of physicians.

we need to better understand the nature of physician wellness, and to develop more effective interventions that will improve the wellbeing of physicians, their patients, their families, their colleagues, and society as a whole.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to focus on the whole physician and the whole person.
we have not been able to help physicians to be resilient.
physicians and trainees must be trained in the skills of resiliency, which include self-awareness, self-regulation, and self-care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to do a better job at helping our trainees and physicians cope with the stresses of our profession.
physicians need to learn to be resilient, to be aware of their own stress, and to learn how to cope with it.
the more we understand about ourselves and how our brains work, the more resilient we will become.
